title: Accessible Components in React ⚛️
description: Build reusable, accessible components with hooks, refs, and props while keeping semantics intact.

slides.title: React & Accessibility: The Basics ⚛️
slides.content:
React does not change HTML semantics – JSX compiles to real HTML. So all your HTML a11y rules apply. The main React‑specific tasks are:

- Using `ref` for focus management.
- Managing `id` for label associations dynamically.
- Conditionally rendering without destroying focus.
- Handling keyboard events correctly.

React's component model encourages reusability – build accessible primitives once.

quizData.question: In React, why might you use a `useRef` for an input element?

options.text: To programmatically focus it after an action

quizData.explanation: Refs allow direct DOM access for focus management and measuring.

slides.title: Handling IDs for Labels & Descriptions 🏷️
useId Hook Example

quizData.question: Why is a unique ID important for accessible forms in a React app?

options.text: To associate labels with inputs across multiple instances of the same component

quizData.explanation: Without unique IDs, all inputs would share the same label association, breaking screen reader navigation.

slides.title: Focus on Mount & Unmount 🔄
Accessible Event Handling ⌨️

quizData.question: A React component has an `onClick` prop but no keyboard handler. Is it accessible?

options.text: No, keyboard users cannot activate it

quizData.explanation: Native buttons handle Enter/Space, but custom elements need explicit key handlers.

slides.title: React A11y Libraries 📚
slides.content:
- **Reach UI** – accessible primitives (dialog, tabs, menu).
- **Radix UI** – unstyled, accessible components.
- **Downshift** – accessible autocomplete/combobox.
- **react‑aria** (Adobe) – hooks for building your own accessible components.

Using well‑tested libraries reduces your implementation burden and ensures correct ARIA and keyboard patterns.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Test components in isolation with Storybook
Use Storybook's accessibility addon (powered by axe) to audit each component separately.
